title: AFCI-Bench v2 Evaluator Manifest (frozen, external)
description: The frozen, externally mounted manifest that tells the architecture-conformance oracle what to evaluate for one task: applicable rule ids, the FROZEN fixed opportunity set (the applicable-opportunity denominator), required/optional/prohibited areas, legitimate-alternative references, manual-rubric and hidden-test references, a checkpoint reference, evaluator content hashes, invalidation status, and the frozen dependency policy the reference checker applies. It is mounted OUTSIDE the coding worktree (see EVALUATOR_MOUNT_POLICY.md). Development scaffolding for study v2: committed instances are templates/synthetic and MUST carry no task-specific answers (answers_populated=false). No paid run produced it.

task_id.description: Task identifier placeholder. Null or a TASK-TEMPLATE-* id in committed templates; a real task id only in externally mounted, private manifests.

status.description: Lifecycle state. The oracle scores ONLY a manifest whose status is exactly 'frozen' and whose invalidation.invalidated is false; every other state fails closed (enforced by the engine, not merely this schema).

e1_analysis_eligibility.description: REQUIRED. Analysis eligibility for the primary endpoint E1, binding this manifest to the approved public task index (experiments/v2/tasks/public/TASK_INDEX.csv and docs/v2/PILOT_PUBLIC_TASK_MATRIX.csv). The engine enforces five FAIL-CLOSED gates: (1) for a real task_id the value must equal the approved public value (ELIGIBILITY_TASK_INDEX_MISMATCH); (2) a 'functional-only' task must contribute NO E1 opportunity denominator (ELIGIBILITY_DENOMINATOR_CONFLICT); (3) an 'inactive-reserve' task enters no E1 run or aggregation unless a separately recorded pre-run activation decision changes its eligibility (ELIGIBILITY_RESERVE_INACTIVE) - it MAY retain draft opportunities, which stay ANALYTICALLY INACTIVE and are reported as a zero denominator rather than deleted; (4) a 'scored' task must have a valid non-zero frozen opportunity denominator before it can enter E1 (ELIGIBILITY_SCORED_WITHOUT_OPPORTUNITIES); (5) any mismatch is an explicit lifecycle/manifest-integrity failure, never a silent rescore or a silent zero. Private per-task manifests predate this field and MUST be migrated before they can be scored.

opportunities.description: The FROZEN fixed opportunity set. Its size is the applicable-opportunity denominator; it is frozen per task manifest and NOT derived from how many files/layers a model touched, how many files it created or edited, or how many imports matched. Each opportunity is ONE architectural decision — a frozen `locator.scope` layer plus the target layers that decision forbids — and carries no expected implementation answer. One frozen opportunity contributes AT MOST ONE violation however many forbidden edges it covers. `rule_id` MUST be the implemented LEAF clause (AR-DEP-002..006) for the declared scope -> forbidden-target relationship; the AR-DEP-001 umbrella may put the whole matrix in force via applicable_rule_ids but may NEVER back a scored opportunity (UMBRELLA_OPPORTUNITY_RULE). opportunity_id MUST be unique across this array — JSON Schema cannot express object-property uniqueness, so the oracle loader is the authoritative guard and fails closed (DUPLICATE_OPPORTUNITY_ID) on any repeat; uniqueItems here is a weaker backstop that only catches fully-identical entries.

locator.description: Where the rule applies. Structural only (architectural scope and forbidden target layers); never an implementation answer. SCORING IS ANCHORED ON THE FROZEN ARCHITECTURAL SCOPE, NOT ON A FILE: the oracle evaluates the opportunity over every source file the frozen dependency_policy.layers path globs assign to `scope`, so a task that legitimately places new implementation code in a different file of the same scope is still scored against the same one opportunity. The engine fails closed (INVALID_OPPORTUNITY_SCOPE / OPPORTUNITY_RULE_SCOPE_MISMATCH / DUPLICATE_OPPORTUNITY_SCOPE / UMBRELLA_OPPORTUNITY_RULE) on a locator it could not score as written.

importer_path.description: PROVENANCE / AUTHORING EVIDENCE ONLY. The file the decision was authored against. It DOES NOT determine scoring: deleting, renaming, or moving it cannot change the opportunity's outcome, and a forbidden edge introduced in any other file of the same frozen scope still violates this opportunity. May be null.

scope.description: SCORING ANCHOR. The `id` of a layer declared in dependency_policy.layers (the layer id, not the catalog `scope:*` tag). Required in practice for a dependency opportunity: the engine refuses (INVALID_OPPORTUNITY_SCOPE) a scope that is null or is not a frozen layer id.

forbidden_target_layers.description: SCORING ANCHOR. The target layers this ONE frozen architectural decision forbids. Every entry must be a known layer id that the frozen `allowed` matrix genuinely forbids for `scope` (a permitted target could never be violated and would pad the E1 denominator with zero exposure). No two opportunities may claim the same (scope, target) decision, so a single forbidden edge is never counted twice.

areas.description: Structural surface areas as path globs. Required/optional/prohibited AREAS (not answers): which parts of the tree the task may touch. Kept out of the coding worktree.

legitimate_alternatives.description: References to accepted legitimate-alternative solution shapes (frozen before confirmatory data). Empty in committed templates (no answers).

evaluator_hashes.description: Map of mounted evaluator file path -> SHA-256, recorded so the run manifest can prove provenance without exposing contents.

dependency_policy.description: Frozen policy the dependency-direction reference checker applies. Repository-architecture-level (same across tasks on a base SHA); NOT a task answer. Layers are assigned by frozen path globs so a model cannot relabel a file by editing tsconfig.

alias_config_path.description: Path, relative to the snapshot root, of the tsconfig whose compilerOptions.paths/baseUrl drive alias resolution.

allowed.description: Map of layer id -> array of allowed target layer ids. Intra-layer and third-party imports are always allowed.

answers_populated.description: MUST be false for any manifest committed to the public repository: committed manifests are templates/synthetic and carry no task-specific answers.
